comment: Declared blind spots, carried into every run directory by hapax.py and shown as a fixed panel in the web view rather than a footnote (SPEC.md 8.3). Each entry names the measurement that established it, so a reader can check the claim rather than take it. A blind spot is removed from this file only when a committed result removes it.

blind_spots.statement: Nothing in this tool detects a molecule present below roughly 1 in a million read pairs.
blind_spots.evidence: results/peptide_absence/ (160,774 false flags per million at the 1-in-a-million operating point); results/spike_abundance/ (geNomad calls nothing below ~2x coverage, assembly breadth 0% at 0.5x)
blind_spots.consequence: A negative for a rare virus is not evidence of absence. Any sensitivity figure quoted without an abundance is unreadable.

blind_spots.statement: Recognition of a relative stops between roughly 10% and 20% nucleotide divergence, and nucleotide indexes stop first.
blind_spots.evidence: results/spike_holdout/ (spike reads surviving tier 1: 0.00% at 0% divergence, 12.6% at 10%, 81.6% at 20%, 99.6% at 30%; at 20% every nucleotide index identifies zero and the protein tiers 18%)
blind_spots.consequence: A read in the residue may be a known organism's homolog at 25% divergence and this tool cannot say so. The protein tier is what holds the ceiling up and must not be dropped for speed.

blind_spots.statement: Two reads from the same genome find each other in the joint space only down to about 1 in 100,000 of the library.
blind_spots.evidence: results/residue_structure/ REPORT.md section 4, 5 seeds (planted-read neighbour purity 99.6% at 1e-3, 10.4% at 1e-5 against a 2.5% control, nothing at 1e-6); results/mate_friends/ gives the mate-linkage upper bound on the same geometry
blind_spots.consequence: Grouping is a statement about abundant residue. For anything rarer the tool reports reads, not groups, and the web view must not draw a group that the wall says cannot exist.

blind_spots.statement: The split-mapping chimaera test fires on 26% of ordinary known background reads, so a read-level chimaera call carries almost no information.
blind_spots.evidence: results/residue_report/ (false-positive rate measured on subtracted reads); results/partial_match_subjects/ (above significance the half-matching shape has no population: matches cover a median 87 of 107 bases and hold identity into the padding)
blind_spots.consequence: Chimaera is reported on contigs, after assembly, and not as a read-level verdict.

blind_spots.statement: Every removal fraction this tool reports is a statement about one library on one day, not about wastewater.
blind_spots.evidence: results/dna_rna_pair/ and results/rrna_content/ (same plant, both RNA, eight months apart: rRNA 38.0% to 67.1%, identifiable 22.7% to 40.7%, virus-identifiable 12.0% to 6.5%)
blind_spots.consequence: Read every cascade percentage as 'on this sample'. A per-sample calibration run sits behind every score for exactly this reason.

blind_spots.statement: A reported fraction without its threshold is unreadable: one database removes 42.8%, 21.7% or 3.5% of the same library depending only on its confidence setting.
blind_spots.consequence: Every number in the run directory carries its operating point, and the web view shows the sweep rather than a single value.

blind_spots.statement: Artefact detection is the weakest load-bearing piece of the tool. If almost everything real matches something, whatever truly matches nothing is mostly artefact, and that is the judgement the tool is least able to make.
blind_spots.evidence: results/subtract_known/ (across four cumulative protein indexes residue 'any hit' goes 77.7 to 98.9%); the chimaera false-positive rate above
blind_spots.consequence: A read with no match anywhere is reported as unplaceable, never as novel.

blind_spots.statement: An index can answer whether something is already known. It cannot answer whether something is new, because score ordering tracks database proximity.
blind_spots.evidence: results/readlevel_features/ (PR #8); results/peptide_absence/ (score ordering put background above spike at every threshold)
blind_spots.consequence: There is no novelty score anywhere in the run directory or the web view. The deliverable is identity-to-closest-relative with its coverage and E-value, and the joint space as a density.

blind_spots.statement: A matched DNA library from the same water does not hold the RNA residue, so a second extraction is not a cheap way to remove background.
blind_spots.evidence: results/dna_rna_pair/ (13.3% of unidentified RNA reads witnessed in the DNA library, less than identified reads' 16.5%; the DNA library is 99.1% unidentified and a phage-dominated virome)
blind_spots.consequence: Cross-library subtraction is not offered. Cross-sample recurrence is a reference, never a subtrahend, because subtracting it would make recurrence circular.

blind_spots.statement: The sample's own assembly is by far the most efficient subtrahend, and that is also what makes it unusable for any recurrence claim.
blind_spots.evidence: results/subtract_known/ (15 MB of the sample's own identified contigs removes 30.33 points on top of 32 GB of Kraken2; 1.4 MB of its own rRNA contigs beats all 272 MB of SILVA)
blind_spots.consequence: What survives subtraction of the sample's own assembly is rare AND unsequenced, which is a narrower and more honest claim than absence from public databases.
